formLanguage: planar printed plate in a folded aluminium tray
objectClass.notes: A bolted roadside sign: a printed plate in a folded aluminium tray on a square post. Nothing hinges, nothing turns and nothing clips into it, so one root pivot and zero sockets is the correct contract. Roadside and soi signage across Thailand: sun-faded printed sheeting in an aluminium tray, a galvanised post rusting at the bracket line and muddy at the foot.

reasoning: TWO components at the 2 draw calls the asset carries: the printed tray (one rounded-rectangle extrude on the sheeting material, its +Z face sampling a baked atlas of the plate's own rectified printed field through planar UVs, every other vertex pinned to a back-tone strip in the same image) and the galvanised support (post, cap plate, channel brackets, vertical spine and the bright rim lip around the tray, merged on one material with height-keyed UVs).

Two materials: sheeting (white, vertex colours, the baked atlas as map) and galvanised steel (white, vertex colours, a height-keyed paint canvas carrying the rust band under the plate, its streaks and the mud wash at the foot).
No repetition system: nothing repeats at this size.
Action readiness: one root pivot at base-centre, zero sockets, one box collider on the root, not breakable.

specDepthDecision.rationale: The identity is the printed face -- a white U-turn arrow hooking to the left over Thai and Latin legends, inside a white border rule -- and the proportion of plate to post. The face is the plate's own pixels rectified into the sign plane, so its grime, fading and lettering are the reference's rather than a redrawn approximation; the tray, lip and post are geometry because their reveals shade themselves.

detailInventory.note: Enumerate every identity-defining small detail before authoring the spec. Each detail must map to a component.localFeatures entry or material.localOverrides entry, never prose only. Use forge/stage1_intake/build_detail_inventory.py to scan zones.

preSpecAssessment.unknownsResolutionNote: Emptied because every entry has been RESOLVED with a recorded authoring decision, not because the gaps went away. Each is restated in assumptions and in viewEvidence with its confidence and a null path. Nothing was invented to close a gap.

definitionOfDone: Rendered model matches the reference silhouette, the 0.90 x 2.40 x 0.14 m proportions, the visible component hierarchy and the material response for a real-time browser prop.
All four scene-budget ceilings hold: <=800 triangles, <=2 draw calls, <=2 materials, <=2 unique geometries.
Zero coincident co-facing surface pairs (check-coplanar clean).
Exactly one root pivot plus 0 named mechanism pivot(s); zero sockets; box collider; no destruction groups.
Every material declares textureless with named evidence.

pivotInventory.name: root
pivotInventory.justification: The rigid body of the prop at its declared origin. A named pivot is a promise that a part turns on it, and only real mechanisms get one.

actionReadiness.socketJustification: ZERO sockets, deliberately. Nothing attaches to this prop and nothing is emitted from it. A marker named for a place on the surface is a location, not a mechanism.

colliderInventory.note: Declared on the asset as box: the sign envelope; the shipped compound is derived from the geometry (plate slab over a post).

actionReadiness.destructionJustification: The asset declares destructionGroups as an empty list -- this prop is NOT breakable. No component carries actionProfile.destruction.fractureGroup. promote-model checks built against declared as an equality in BOTH directions, so an invented group fails the gate just as a missing one would.

assumptions: The printed face is the plate's own rectified field: what the reference shows is what ships, including its grime and fading.
The back of the plate and the brackets are not in the plate; a channel-bracket mounting is assumed, which is how every Thai roadside tray sign is hung.
The plate crops the post at the frame edge, so the post's ground contact is built to the declared height rather than observed.

coordinateFrame.notes: Origin base-center at ground, +Y up, +Z the FRONT face (the face the plate shows).

silhouette.description: A 0.9 x 1.2 m blue rounded plate over a 0.09 m square post 2.3 m tall; the plate occupies the top half of the 2.4 m and the post is the only thing below it.
silhouette.envelopeDerivation: Plate 0.9 x 1.2 m at y 1.2..2.4 (declared). The plate's printed field corners read (401,179) (652,101) (631,494) (416,595); the near edge is 416 px for 1.2 m. The post reads 48 px wide at y 700 = 0.138 m across two faces of a square section, i.e. 0.09-0.10 m square, and the Meshy proxy reads it at 4 of 24 plate-width columns (0.167 of 0.9 = 0.15 m at voxel resolution); built 0.09 m square. Depth: post 0.09 + brackets 0.012 + tray 0.033 + lip 0.008 = 0.14 m (declaration corrected from 0.08). Margin 0.025 m and rule 0.022 m read at row 400 (blue 390-398, rule 400-406) and column 430 (blue 148-156, rule 158-166) at ~294 px/m.
silhouette.meshyCrossCheck: Meshy v7 proxy (scratch/u-turn-sign/reference.glb) normalises the plate to 0.45 H tall and 0.31 H wide (w/h 0.69 against the declared 0.75) with the post at 0.052 H wide and 0.55 H below the plate -- the post is cropped by the plate frame, so its total height is not observable; the plate/post width ratio (0.167) is the number taken from it.

viewEvidence.note: NOT DIRECTLY OBSERVED. Confidence 0.80: the back of a tray sign is bare aluminium over channel brackets on the post; built that way and pinned to a back-tone texel.

componentTree.name: Printed sign plate
componentTree.topologyRationale: One rounded-rectangle extrude on the sheeting material: the printed face is a texture, so the tray is the only geometry the material needs.

geometryDescriptor.topologyIntent: Rounded-rectangle tray 0.9 x 1.2 m, 33 mm deep, standing on the brackets in front of the post; its front face carries the atlas.
geometryDescriptor.zFightingNote: The tray front is 4 mm BEHIND the rim lip's front and the lip ring overlaps the tray edge by 20 mm, so the two never share a plane; the tray back butts the spine and brackets as an OPPOSED joint.
geometryDescriptor.mergeNote: One extrude; +Z vertices take planar atlas UVs, all others pin to one texel.

colorMaterialRecipe.recipe: White sheeting material; the +Z face samples the baked front atlas planarly (base white), every other vertex pins to the atlas's back-tone strip and keeps its aluminium vertex tint.

actionProfile.notes: Rigidly parented to the root. NO pivot and NO socket, deliberately: this part does not move and nothing attaches to it.

componentTree.name: Galvanised post, brackets and rim lip
componentTree.topologyRationale: Post, cap plate, two channel brackets, a vertical spine and the rim-lip ring merged on one material: the second draw call.

geometryDescriptor.topologyIntent: Post 0.09 m square from y 0 to 2.30 with a cap plate; two 0.56 m channel brackets and a vertical spine between the post and the tray; the rim lip a 20 mm rounded ring 8 mm proud of the tray face.
geometryDescriptor.zFightingNote: Brackets and spine stand between post face and tray back as opposed butt joints; the lip ring overlaps the tray edge; the cap plate sits 4 mm above the post top.
geometryDescriptor.mergeNote: One merged BufferGeometry with height UVs at 2.4 m.

colorMaterialRecipe.recipe: White galvanised material with a height-keyed paint canvas; the post and brackets white-tinted, the rim lip tinted bright, a mud axis tint over the foot.

pivot.name: root
pivot.notes: At the origin the asset declares. A STATIC prop: nothing opens, turns or swings, so one root pivot is the whole mechanism inventory and that is the correct answer, not a gap.

collider.notes: Declared on the asset as box: the sign envelope; the shipped compound is derived from the geometry (plate slab over a post).

roughness.notes: Scalar observed for this surface in the plate. The independently extracted map is kept on disk as evidence and is NOT bound at runtime -- this material is textureless, so the scalar is the runtime value.

albedo.samplingNotes: Measured as the mean of crops/field.png. extract_pbr_evidence confidence 0.900. The extractor palette is advisory only: these crops are flat material swatches, not isolated objects, so its foreground separation is weak by its own warnings. Albedo is the direct crop measurement.

localOverrides.evidence: crops/legend.png and crops/field.png -- the fading, grime and speckle are carried by the rectified plate pixels themselves in the front atlas.

evidence: Measured on viewEvidence region-field: the clean blue field between the arrow and the rule reads #2f66a2 (rows 400-410 at x 408-440, #2c649f..#3169a6); the atlas carries the plate pixels themselves so the field ships at the plate's value.
Border rule and legend #c3c4c2..#c7c7c5 (row 400 x 400-406, the rule); the arrow crown reads brighter where it is clean and grey where the plate's grime sits on it, and both arrive through the atlas.

Textureless as DECLARED: the face is one baked WebP atlas bound after construction (the plate's rectified field inside a drawn margin and border rule, plus a back-tone strip every non-front vertex pins to), on a WHITE material with white front vertex colours so the atlas's own colours ship.
textureless.note: Declared textureless so createSculptMaterial skips makeProceduralTextureSet entirely -- FIVE canvases per material written pixel by pixel, at a cost that is the SQUARE of the resolution. It is also a correctness fix: with a texture set the generator forces color to white and roughness to 1 and reads both from the generated maps, discarding this measured albedo.

roughness.notes: Scalar observed for this surface in the plate. The independently extracted map is kept on disk as evidence and is NOT bound at runtime -- this material is textureless, so the scalar is the runtime value.

localOverrides.region: post top under the plate, and the foot 0-0.30 m
localOverrides.evidence: crops/rust.png -- the mud-and-rust foot; the rust band under the plate is read on the plate at the bracket line.

evidence: Measured on viewEvidence region-post at #747b7f (luma 121, plate x 500-525 y 640-760): the harness side-lit transfer for this build measured 0.6 x authored (168 -> 101), so the canvas base is authored at #c7ccd1 and the post returns #8b847b luma 133 at azimuth 0.

Rust at the bracket line: the plate reads brown #664d39..#87674e from the plate's bottom edge for ~35 px (0.12 m) at x 520, then galvanised from y 600. Carried as an hband at v 0.452-0.50 of the 2.4 m height canvas with 36 streaks hanging from it, and the foot as a ground band plus a mud axis tint (#a89070, sat 0.33) over 0.03-0.32 m.
Textureless as DECLARED: one 512 px paint canvas after construction, height-keyed over the whole 2.4 m (uvScale 2.4) so the rust band lands under the plate and the mud wash at the foot, once each.

reviewHistory.summary: FINAL VERDICT. Overall visual fidelity 0.92 -- the five layers mean 0.904 and the four critical features 0.915. 248/800 triangles, 2/2 draw calls, 2/2 materials, 2/2 unique geometries, one 21.8 KB baked atlas and one 512 px canvas (2.9 MB texture VRAM), 68 ms to construct.

lodPlan.strategy: full component tree and material layers
merge static components and reduce local feature geometry

performanceBudget.optimizationPolicy: Real-time browser FPS prop on low-end integrated GPUs; a level builder places hundreds at once. All four ceilings come from thaikit resolveBudget() for the small class and none was invented. The component split was costed against the DRAW-CALL ceiling in the blockout, before any geometry existed: parts that share a material are merged into one component rather than left to be merged later, because a pivot hung off a part cannot be merged afterwards.

materials.note: sheeting and galv: 2 of 2; aluminium back, lip and mud as vertex tints.

uniqueGeometries.note: One per component plus one per repetition system. A scaled box is NOT a shared geometry -- the generator bakes real dimensions in via geometry.scale(), so every differently-sized box is genuinely distinct. Each InstancedMesh reuses a single geometry across all its instances, which is the whole point.

triangles.note: 248 of 800: one 16-point rounded extrude (60), one 32-point ring extrude (128), six boxes.

lightingFromPhoto.notes: The plate is a flat studio lightbox: surfaces at 90 degrees to each other measure within a few levels, which is only possible under near-shadowless illumination. That is WHY the measured crop means are usable as albedo with little correction.
High fill ratio inferred from the shadow-side wall retaining full value.

The seamless backdrop acts as a large uniform environment. The thaikit harness supplies NO environment map, which is why every metal on this prop carries a metalness well below its physical value -- a metal with nothing to reflect renders black.
NO rim light in the plate. Recorded so a missing rim in the render is not read as a defect.
Exposure 1.0 with ACES filmic tone mapping; no exposure compensation is applied to the measured albedos and none is warranted.

NO contact or ground shadow in the plate -- it is a cut-out against a seamless backdrop. Recorded so the absence is not read as a missing feature. IN USE this is a floor-placed building and the HOST scene owns its contact shadow: castShadow ships enabled on every mesh and the factory defines no ground plane of its own.

proceduralStrategy.strategy: A rounded-rectangle extrude for the tray, a ring extrude for the rim lip, boxes for the post, cap, brackets and spine.
No InstancedMesh: nothing repeats. A level instances whole signs.
All procedural variation is assigned by instance INDEX, never from a random source, so the model is byte-identical on every build.
Both materials are declared textureless. One baked front atlas (WebP data URI, ~22 KB) and one 512 px paint canvas after construction, both guarded for plain Node.

risks.description: The rectified field is ~250 plate pixels wide, upsampled to 512 px/m.
risks.mitigation: Legends read at prop distance; the soft edge is the plate's own.

risks.description: The plate crops the post; its foot is not observed.
risks.mitigation: Built to the declared height with a mud wash keyed to the foot.
